AGRICULTURE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any white crystal used in cooking
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

2. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Producers
   D. Tertiary consumers

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Ice melting to water

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Preparing Animal Products? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Preparing Animal Products.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Preparing Animal Products.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Preparing Animal Products.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Constructing Water Retention Structures? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Constructing Water Retention Structures.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Establishment Planting Site? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Establishment Planting Site.

7. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Selected Crop Management Practises? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Selected Crop Management Practises.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Selected Crop Management Practises.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Selected Crop Management Practises.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Selected Crop Management Practises.

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Glucose and oxygen
   D. Only water vapour

10. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

11. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Cooking Food? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Cooking Food.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Cooking Food.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Cooking Food.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Making Homemade Soap 8 Total Number of Lessons 120 Note: The suggested number of and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Making Homemade Soap and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Controlling Soil Pollution and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Constructing Water Retention Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

2. C — Producers

3. D — Ice melting to water

4. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Preparing Animal Products.

5. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Constructing Water Retention Structures.

6. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Establishment Planting Site.

7. D — 100 °C

8. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Selected Crop Management Practises.

9. C — Glucose and oxygen

10. B — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

11. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

12. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Cooking Food.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Making Homemade Soap 8 Total Number of Lessons 120 Note: The suggested number of; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Making Homemade Soap; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Controlling Soil Pollution; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Constructing Water Retention Structures; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
